semantic_contract: Build one default-constructed 0x14-byte POD in the local frame and immediately hand it, together with the registry singleton, the caller's key and the caller's mode, to 0x0045ac20. The wrapper itself is unconditional: no branch, no global read, no field write, no error path and no return value. Everything the caller can observe -- object creation through vtable slot +0x2c of a manager, transform assignment through slot +0x18, a detach through slot +0x8, and the map swap guarded by 'mode == 1' -- happens one frame deeper. The receiver is not the cEditor: it is the global pointer at 0x015d0c14, returned by the argument-ignoring getter 0x00401050, and the cEditor only supplies the key and the mode. The first argument is always the same value the caller handed to 0x00401050, which the getter discards.
classification_rationale: The wrapper's own contract is fully observed -- 17 instructions, no branch, two direct calls, exact push order -- so the STRUCTURAL_ONLY floor is clearly cleared. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because three material elements are bounded rather than established, and each is named: (1) the registry type behind 0x015d0c14 is unknown, no vtable was located and the file-image value is zero; (2) the 0x14-byte POD has a proven byte layout but no proven meaning, and its three data-sourced dwords are zero in the image so their runtime values are unobservable; (3) the four virtual slots 0x0045ac20 dispatches through have no concrete callee, because the receiver types are only known at runtime. A further observed defect -- three arguments pushed into a four-argument callee -- is recorded rather than resolved, since resolving it would require inventing a value for the gap.
semantic_findings: 0x0045ae10 is a two-line forwarder: default-POD construction, then delegation. It has no branch of any kind.

The receiver is the global singleton at 0x015d0c14, not the cEditor. 0x00401050 ignores its argument entirely (MOV EAX,[0x015d0c14]; RET), so the 'PUSH <id>; CALL 0x00401050' idiom at every inspected callsite is a singleton fetch, and the id is really the first argument of 0x0045ae10.

Both inspected callsites are Editors::cEditor methods (OnMouseDown and SetActiveMode), and the cEditor supplies only the key (0x3f1bf51, or cEditor + 0x27c) and the mode (a scratch register, or the literal 1).

The local POD is 0x14 bytes: 4 zero bytes, three dwords copied from .data globals, and the literal 1.0f. A 1.0f default alongside three copied values is transform-like, but no SDK type was matched and none is claimed.

The three .data globals feeding the POD (0x015d22f0/f4/f8) and the one passed by address to 0x0041cb40 (0x015d2638) are all zero in the file image, so the shipped build fills them at start-up and their values cannot be recovered statically.
0x0045ac20 walks the same hash map at the same receiver + 0x8 offset that 0x0045b150 erases from, so the two targets share one registry object.

Virtual slots +0x0, +0x4 and +0x8 behave as destructor / attach / detach consistently across five independent bodies in this batch (0x0045ac20, 0x005c1dc0, 0x005c8480, 0x00573c00, 0x005c8480 grow arm). That consistency is an observation about slot behaviour, not a name.

The wrapper under-supplies 0x0045ac20 by one stack argument. The gap is read at 0x0045acf6 and is reachable because the SetActiveMode callsite passes mode = 1, which is the value 0x0045ace3 tests for.
unresolved_questions: What is the type behind 0x015d0c14? The file image holds zero, no vtable was located, and the SDK has no matching global manager for this access pattern.
What is the 0x14-byte POD built by 0x00434040? Its bytes are known; its type, alignment intent and units are not. The 1.0f default suggests a scale but proves nothing.
What do 0x015d22f0/f4/f8 hold at runtime, and what does 0x0041cb40(&0x015d2638) do with them?

Why does this wrapper pass three arguments to a four-argument callee? Either 0x0045ac20's fourth parameter is genuinely optional in practice, or the observed build reads an uninitialised slot. Static evidence cannot decide between those.

What are the four virtual slots 0x0045ac20 uses (+0x2c on a manager, +0x18 and +0x08 on the created object, +0x00/+0x04 on the map-resident object)? Slot offsets are observed; names and owning interfaces are not.
Is 0x0045ae10 an inline expansion of a one-line source function, or a real out-of-line wrapper? Its 42-byte body and 13-call fan-in are consistent with either.
The 13 callers are only 2 inspected. The other 11 pass their key and mode through registers whose provenance was not traced, so the argument distribution across the fan-in is not established.
confidence_note: confidence in the per-aspect claim, not a probability of behavioural equivalence with any shipped source
